deepResearch.intro: Austin-area drivers should start with the court printed on the citation and receive permission before enrolling. TxDOT reports 10,791 total reportable crashes in Austin in 2024, including 91 fatal crashes resulting in 98 fatalities and 349 suspected-serious-injury crashes resulting in 400 suspected serious injuries. Its separate city table reports 916 DUI-alcohol crashes, including 19 fatal crashes resulting in 21 fatalities and 43 suspected-serious-injury crashes resulting in 56 suspected serious injuries. These traffic figures do not determine DSC eligibility. Use only the card for the court named on your citation.

hub.summary: For a citation filed in Austin Municipal Court, request DSC before the initial appearance date and wait for court approval. The current form requires the official request, insurance, a non-commercial Texas license or qualifying military proof, and $144 or $169 for a school-zone offense. After processing, return the certificate naming Austin Municipal Court and a DPS Type 3 or 3A record within 90 days.

deepResearch.intro: Beaumont-area drivers should start with the exact court, precinct and place printed on the citation and receive permission before enrolling. TxDOT's 2024 city table reports 3,926 total reportable crashes in Beaumont, including 20 fatal crashes resulting in 21 fatalities and 100 suspected-serious-injury crashes resulting in 116 suspected serious injuries. Its separate city table reports 59 DUI-alcohol crashes, including 2 fatal crashes and 3 suspected-serious-injury crashes. These city traffic figures do not determine DSC eligibility. Use only the card for the court named on your citation.

hub.name: Beaumont
hub.summary: If the citation names Beaumont Municipal Court, ask the court for permission before the appearance date and before enrolling. Submit the required plea, Texas license, insurance showing the defendant as covered and the amount the court currently assesses. The court gives 90 days for a state-approved course and the required DPS driving record. The court still links an application marked 09/2011, so confirm the current amount and requirements before using it.
steps: Confirm that the citation names Beaumont Municipal Court and request DSC before the appearance date.

TxDOT's 2024 city table reports 66,236 total crashes in Houston, including 318 fatal crashes resulting in 339 fatalities and 1,304 suspected-serious-injury crashes resulting in 1,519 suspected serious injuries. Its separate DUI-alcohol city table reports 2,113 crashes, including 91 fatal crashes resulting in 104 fatalities and 80 suspected-serious-injury crashes resulting in 113 suspected serious injuries. deepResearch.intro: Midland-Odessa drivers should start with the exact court printed on the citation. TxDOT's separate 2024 city rows report 6,288 total crashes across Midland and Odessa. Midland recorded 2,704 total crashes, including 19 fatal crashes that resulted in 20 fatalities and 60 suspected-serious-injury crashes that resulted in 68 suspected serious injuries. Odessa recorded 3,584 total crashes, including 28 fatal crashes that resulted in 29 fatalities and 65 suspected-serious-injury crashes that resulted in 76 suspected serious injuries. The separate DUI-alcohol rows report 389 total crashes: Midland recorded 182, including 1 fatal crash that resulted in 1 fatality and 11 suspected-serious-injury crashes that resulted in 15 suspected serious injuries; Odessa recorded 207, including 6 fatal crashes that resulted in 7 fatalities and 13 suspected-serious-injury crashes that resulted in 18 suspected serious injuries. These are separate crash-event and resulting-person measures; they do not determine DSC eligibility or assign a court. A Midland Municipal Court citation and an Odessa Municipal Court citation follow different processes, so use only the card for the exact named municipal court or county precinct printed on your citation.

verbatim.intro: If you receive a citation for a moving traffic violation, you may be able to prevent it from appearing on your driving record by completing a Driving Safety Course. To qualify for this option:
eligibility: You must possess a valid Texas driver's license and current liability insurance;
Can only be granted for one moving violation on the citation;
You must not have taken a Driving Safety Course in the past 12 months;
Could not have been speeding 25 miles or more over the designated speed limit; or
Could not have been speeding at 95 miles per hour or more; or
You must enter an appearance on the citation within 10 days from the issuance date of the citation.
You cannot possess a commerical driver's license.
verbatim.request_intro: You may request this option, by mail, online or by appearance in person, before the Municipal Court within 10 calendar days (not 10 working days) from the date you were issued the citation. You must present the following items to the Municipal Court:
request_items: A plea of “No Contest” and the request to take a Driving Safety Course, either in writing (with your signature), which a space for your written request is provided for your selection on the back of the copy of the citation issued to you, or your appearance in person;
A copy of your valid Texas Driver’s License;
A copy of proof of current liability insurance - the proof of insurance must be in the name of the person that received the citation.
You must submit a $144.00 fee or $169.00 if in a school zone, at the time you request to take the Driving Safety Course.
verbatim.mail_note: All of the above items must be presented at the time of the request to take a Driving Safety Course for this option to be granted by the court. You can mail all of the above to:
verbatim.return_note: If mailing the above items, please be sure to include your name and address so the Order Granting the Driving Safety Course document can be returned to you with the compliance requirements and compliance due date.
verbatim.completion_intro: After the court grants the Driving Safety Course, you must meet the two following compliance requirements.
completion_items: Take a Driving Safety Course within 90 days from the date the Order Granting the Driving Safety Course from a state certified instructor and return with your signature the certificate designated “Court Copy”. You will receive two certificates after completing the Driving Safety Course and the “Insurance Copy” is not to be returned to the court.

Request a certified copy of your driving record from the Driver Records Bureau, Texas Department of Public Safety, P. O. Box 15999, Austin, Texas 78761-5999. This request must be mailed with a $10.00 fee, check or money order, made payable to the Texas Department of Public Safety. Please request the certified copy of your driving record be mailed to you and not to the court so you know the certified copy of your driving record has been received per your request.
verbatim.closing: The above two items must be returned to the court by your due date (the due date is on your Order Granting the Driving Safety Course document) for the violation to be dismissed and prevented from appearing on your driving record.

sub_localities.summary: If the citation names a Wichita County Justice Court, use the exact precinct and place printed on it. The county has five separate Justice Courts and does not publish one uniform countywide DSC process, so contact only the named office before paying or enrolling.
steps: Match the exact Wichita County precinct and place printed on the citation. Do not select a court from your city, ZIP code, address or proximity.
Call only that named office for its current DSC eligibility, request documents, costs and deadlines before paying or taking a course.
For Precinct 2, confirm the current mailing address because its page notes a temporary address during construction.
